provenance: New source translation with E4230-E4239 and E4320-E4329 reviewed.
context: Fiore opens sea-creature boxes, finding apparent junk. Squid riddle, Japanese shrimp etymology riddle, and shadow riddle.
decisions: Shrimp etymology explicitly labeled Japanese so the English question remains meaningful; ebi-iro transliterated. All choice answers and numeric squid clues retained. Spoken teasing preserved.

translations.en: Inside the box was a rather large bottle.
It contained a strange substance, a mixture of thick liquid
and solid matter.
What is this...?
It's kind of gross...
Some sort of medicine? If we have @7rAnselm@0r appraise it,
it could turn out to be something good, right?
I'll hold on to it for now.
Somehow... I'd like to think I'm imagining it, but...
Is it just me, or was all of it junk?
Bottles full of muck, rusty equipment, broken glass...
A-anyway, let's have @7rAnselm@0r appraise it!
Th-the adventure isn't over until we get the results!
Come on, come on! Let's go to the tavern!
Bzzzt! Completely wrong!
You'd see if you took a good look at a squid.
Some of those things are a different length, you know.
They say an octopus has eight legs and a squid has ten,
but think about it. You can try subtraction, too.
It's something a squid has that an octopus doesn't.
That's your hint for the subtraction.
And you'd see if you took a good look at a squid.
You found a treasure chest with a squid drawn on its lid
and the word Inktvis carved beside it.
So Inktvis meant squid?
Just as you reached that conclusion, the box began speaking.
Answer my question and you can have what's inside.
An octopus has eight legs. How many hands does a squid have?
A squid's hands? Squid have hands?
Don't people usually say they have ten legs?
Now, how many hands?
Garnalen Box
Have you figured it out?
What fruit gave the Japanese word for shrimp its name?
Persimmon
Strawberry
Grape
Bzzzt! Wrong, wrong!
It's not persimmon!
I said something that grows in bunches!
And it's a fruit famous for being made into alcohol!
It's not strawberry!
Did the red color of strawberries make you think of shrimp?
But shrimp aren't that red!
When shrimp are bright red,
it's usually because they've been boiled!
Ding ding ding! Absolutely right!
Long ago, "grape color" could be read as ebi-iro, or "shrimp color," too!
Some say it's because shrimp down on the seabed
looked grape-colored. There are various theories.
In fact, large shrimp really do have a grape-like color.
Now, let's open the box!
When the box opened, it revealed something that looked like junk:
what appeared to be parts of unfinished armor.
W-well... These things happen.
But you never know...
I'll take it along, just in case.
A shrimp was drawn on the box.
Beneath it, the word Garnalen was carved.
Apparently, Garnalen meant shrimp.
Hello there! If you want the box opened, answer my question!
Did you know the Japanese word for shrimp comes from a fruit
or the word for its color?
It's a fruit used to make alcohol, and it's delicious to eat, too.
What fruit is it?
A fruit...? Is there some fruit with whiskers like those
and all those wriggly legs?
It's not that sort of fruit! Though it does come in bunches.
Now, answer my question!
Zalm Box
Have you finally figured it out?
However far you travel, even when you're all alone,
what friend always stays beside you and follows you?
A ghost
Your shadow
The sun
Bzzzt! It's not a supernatural phenomenon!
Has anyone ever told you that you don't listen?
I said a friend that always follows you!
Or is a ghost haunting you?
